answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, released only after three unrelated confirmations, rewards vest against future work. The velvet of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Work waits on the anchor until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the whisper of the next round. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
